html:
Tehran became the capital of Iran in 1786, when Agha Mohammad Khan, founder of the Qajar dynasty, made the small walled town south of the Alborz mountains his seat. It has been the capital ever since.

The Qajars built palaces such as the Golestan. Under Reza Shah in the 1920s and 1930s the old walls came down and wide avenues, ministries and a university went up. With the oil boom it grew fast, and today the city has about nine million people and the wider area many more.

Tehran was the centre of the Iranian Revolution in 1979 and of protests from 2009 to the Woman, Life, Freedom movement of 2022. It suffers from smog, traffic and a high risk of earthquakes. See also Iran.
